thread:
mike_dev: Heads-up — I repro'd a ~2.1x perf regression on SM90 for the fused-paged attention case at seq=4096 when the selector picks Triton kernels instead of our CUDA fused kernel. Repro + quick profile below.

maya_infra: ugh, thanks for flagging. which CUDA / Triton versions? can you paste the exact command you used? :eyes:

mike_dev: command I ran:
```bash
python benchmarks/bench_attn.py --model gpt-j-6B --seq_len 4096 --batch 1 --kernel_selector flash_triton,fused_cuda --cuda_version 12.3 --triton_version 2.2 --paged_kv on
```
outputs (microbench avg of 10 runs):
- fused_cuda (our CUDA kernel): 11.8 ms per forward
- triton_flash_variant: 25.4 ms per forward
- baseline old-paged (fallback): 34.1 ms

raj_perf: whoa that's real. did you capture nvtx/nvprof slices? could be memory copies from KV page eviction on SM90.

mike_dev: yes nvprof snapshot attached (trimmed):
```
--- CUDA fused run ---
GPU kernel time: 10.9 ms
device memcpy H2D: 0.2 ms
device memcpy D2H: 0.1 ms
SM occupancy: 72%

--- Triton run ---
Triton kernel (flashx_main): 23.3 ms
device memcpy D2H: 2.5 ms (small repeated spikes)
SM occupancy: 64%
```
Looks like Triton path is doing small synchronous memcpy spikes between some layers — likely due to our paged-KV boundary handling where Triton kernel expects contiguous KV on-device and we end up doing device->host roundtrips for swapped pages.

sasha_research: that matches something I saw last week: Triton kernels in our build do a kernel->host handshake when page count crosses a threshold. On SM80 that handshake was masked by better latency; on SM90 it shows up. Could be a different default async memcpy behavior in CUDA 12.3.

alex_ops: any quick mitigation? a selector fallback or policy we can flip while we fix kernel-handling?

mike_dev: short-term: add heuristic in kernel selector to prefer fused_cuda for seq_len>=2048 on SM90 with paged_kv enabled and CUDA>=12.2. Also disable Triton flash variant for batch_size=1, seq>=2048. That reduces regression to 1.02x vs fused cuda.

maya_infra: can we make that a config flag so customers don't get surprised? we'll toggle in  infra config and ship canary.

raj_perf: long-term fix: stop synchronous D2H in paged-KV path — keep page residency on-device and implement async prefetch for upcoming layers. I can prototype a prefetch window (k = 2 layers ahead) and measure.

mike_dev: I started a small patch: kernel_selector change + a test in benchmarks/ci/sm90_compat. Also added an nvprof wrapper so CI collects tiny memcpy histograms.

ci-bot: CI run triggered: nightly/bench-sm90-compat (job id bk-9091). Will post results when complete. :robot_face:

alex_ops: also file to track is infra-gpu-image: some nodes on canary are running CUDA 12.1, others 12.3; selector must consider runtime CUDA.

sasha_research: note for the perf board: Triton may still be better for short sequences and large batches; don't remove it entirely. We should expand selector rules: (1) seq<1024 => triton_flash preferred for batch>=4, (2) seq>=2048 & batch<=2 => fused_cuda preferred, (3) paged_kv enabled => bias towards CUDA fused if any memcpy spikes observed.

mike_dev: I'll open a PR with tests + selector flag. Patch will include:
- new env var REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL_PREFERENCE="fused_cuda:seq>=2048"
- CI microbench harness update to record memcpy spikes (>0.5ms) count
- NVPROF parser update to detect device->host synchronous memcpy patterns

maya_infra: plan: roll the config to 10% of canary fleet tonight, monitor tail latency and memcpy histogram. If <5% regression we keep; else revert.

raj_perf: add one more check: compare FLOP-util and SM occupancy per kernel. Triton path had lower occupancy which surprised me — maybe kernel launch grid params mismatch on SM90. We should also validate our kernel compile flags for triton builds.

mike_dev: agreed. I'll collect ptx.sass and triton-generated kernel metadata and drop into the perf folder.

maya_infra: thanks all. If anyone can triage the small memcpy source (is it our allocator, cudaMemcpyAsync misuse, or Triton boundary) please add notes to the PR.

sasha_research: I'll look at Triton kernel wrapper; raj can prototype async prefetch. We can revert selector change if we find a proper Triton fix in ~48h. :thumbsup:

alex_ops: logging action item: add a per-model / per-region selector override so enterprise customers can lock to a kernel variant until we ship a formal fix.

mike_dev: filing the PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/PR-4821 — includes benchmark traces and nvprof samples.

ci-bot: PR lint + bench triggered: PR-4821/lint (ok), PR-4821/bench-sm90-compat (running)

maya_infra: good work — let's keep the rollout conservative. thanks for quick detective work. :rocket:
